_note: The living map of Salt Bell (map_life.json, file reference ch. 18): who moves on the pans, what calls on the radio, and what glints beside the roads. Kind and template ids carry the sb_ prefix like everything else; 'behaviour' picks the rule set. Images are bare stems under assets/life/ — a stem the mod does not ship falls back to the base game's picture of the same name.

sb_salt_patrol.name: {0} salt patrol
sb_salt_patrol.desc: Two rigs with mirror-glare goggles and a gun under a bleached tarp. Salt patrols keep their faction's pans clear of anyone whose flag they do not like — which, depending on your standing, includes you.

sb_brine_caravan.name: {0} brine caravan
sb_brine_caravan.desc: A tanker of well water and a trailer of salt blocks, a trader in a wide hat who weighs everything twice. Caravans run between the well and the Hulk while the pans hold — and deal on the road, for a fair price or a fair fight.

sb_salt_pilgrims.name: Salt pilgrims
sb_salt_pilgrims.desc: Bell Folk on foot with white-crusted boots, walking the pans to hear the bell that no longer rings. They carry water for three days and stories for thirty.

sb_hull_pickers.name: Hull pickers
sb_hull_pickers.desc: A crane truck and a cutting crew from the stranded ships, selling plate and rivets by the sack. They know every hull on the pans — and which ones still have something inside.

templates.title: SOS — rig on the pans
templates.intercom: …anyone on the {0}? Broke an axle on the crust near the {1}. The glare is cooking me and the water is going. I'll flash a mirror at noon every day I've got left.
templates.body: A weak voice on the open band. A rig broke down on the pans and its driver is counting water. Drive that road in time and the rig comes with you — damaged, but a rig — and a driver who owes you a life.
templates.claimed: The mirror flash finds you before you find the rig. The driver has built a sunshade from a door and is sitting under it with the last half-can, saving it for you, she says, as if that made sense.
templates.expired: The mirror on the {0} did not flash at noon. The pans keep what they take.

templates.title: Bounty — mirror riders
templates.intercom: {2} · {3}: riders have made camp on the {0}, near the {1}, signalling each other with mirrors and stopping our water. Break them before the next caravan and the house pays.
templates.body: A faction has posted a bounty on a gang camped along that road. Drive it within the time, fight them on the crust, win — and the reward is wired to your position, with a note in the faction's ledger.
templates.claimed: You see the mirror flashes long before you see the rigs. They see yours too.
templates.expired: The riders on the {0} moved on before anyone came. The bounty is withdrawn.

templates.title: Radar ping — under the crust
templates.intercom: Radar off the {0}, near the {1}: a hard square return a metre under the crust. Something sank into the pan when it was still wet, and the salt kept it.
templates.body: Something square and metal lies a metre under the salt crust off that road — a container from the days when the pans were a sea. Whoever digs first keeps it.
templates.claimed: The crust breaks like sugar and the corner of a shipping container comes up white with salt. The seal is intact.
templates.expired: A hole in the crust off the {0}, fresh tire tracks around it. Someone was faster.

templates.name: Salt-crusted camp
templates.lore: Two tents collapsed under a crust of salt, a fire ring, a cooking pot white to the rim. A note weighted with a salt block: 'Truck's dead in the sink south of here. Take what's in the bed, we couldn't.' Boot prints lead north, toward the bell that does not ring.
templates.linkText: The note names a truck in the sink to the south.

templates.name: Truck in the sink
templates.lore: The truck went through the crust to its axles and stayed there, engine seized by brine. The bed is above the salt and nobody came back for it: four spare tires under a bleached tarp and two ammunition crates, the seals intact.

templates.name: Ship's bell in the hull
templates.lore: A stranded coaster lying on its side, and in the wheelhouse a small brass bell nobody took, rung once by the wind while you stand there. Chalked on the bulkhead beside it, a chart of the pans with a course plotted to a place your map does not show.

templates.name: Pilgrims' shrine
templates.lore: A cairn of salt blocks with a cracked bell painted on the top stone. Pilgrims leave what they can spare: bottle caps, a shoe, a photograph gone white. A locked offering box is chained to the cairn. The key hangs on the far side, where only somebody who walks around it will look.
templates.linkText: The key to the offering box hangs on the far side of the cairn.

templates.name: Offering box
templates.lore: The box holds what pilgrims leave for pilgrims: sealed water bottles, more than you expected, and a note that says only 'for the next one'. You are the next one. You leave two bottles and take the rest.

templates.name: Dry-dock crane
templates.lore: A dock crane standing on the pans where the harbour used to be, its hook swinging over nothing. The cab still holds the rigger's toolbox: bolts, rivets and a bag of machine screws in oil paper, kept by the salt like a fossil.

templates.name: Mirror rider's wreck
templates.lore: A rider's buggy on its roof, a signal mirror still bolted to the roll cage. The rider is gone. Scratched into the paint of the door: an arrow and a number of paces. Riders cache what they cannot carry.
templates.linkText: An arrow and a number of paces scratched into the door.

templates.name: Rider's cache
templates.lore: Forty paces from the wreck, a salt block that is not a salt block: a wooden box painted white. Inside, resistors in a sock, a roll of sheet metal and a spare mirror. The riders will know somebody counted the paces.

templates.name: Old evaporator
templates.lore: A pre-collapse evaporator pond with its pipes still standing, and in the last pipe a tap that somebody keeps in order. Fresh water, warm, tasting of iron. A tin cup on a chain. You fill every can you own.
